headline: Highest risk is medium: OpenBBTerminal can ingest MCP/API content while pathway is local-only, creating prompt-injection and data-handling exposure; no direct evidence of a dangerous default pairwise bridge.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenBBTerminal exposes MCP/REST/FastAPI surfaces and has a sandboxing pattern of “connect once, consume everywhere,” so it can ingest external content that may be treated as trusted. pathway has no clipboard/screen capture and no MCP, so the pair lacks a documented direct bridge, but OpenBBTerminal’s own ingestion surfaces make injection plausible in default integrations.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal consumes untrusted MCP/API payloads as instructions or prompts, injection becomes active.
IF pathway is inserted as an upstream document source into OpenBBTerminal without provenance checks, malicious content can propagate.
mitigations: Disable MCP/API ingestion for untrusted sources.
Add provenance tags to all inbound documents.
Strip instruction-like text before passing outputs onward.
Review one sample pipeline for prompt-like tokens.
requires-engineering: add allowlist-based content parsing.

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenBBTerminal touches financial, licensed, and public data, while pathway’s profile shows no data classes touched and no filesystem or network egress. There is no shared workspace or authenticated principal documented, so leakage between the pair is not evidenced; the main concern is accidental exposure if operators manually bridge OpenBBTerminal outputs into pathway workflows.
conditions: IF operators copy OpenBBTerminal outputs containing financial or licensed data into pathway inputs, leakage occurs.
IF both agents are later deployed under a shared workspace or shared credentials, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Keep separate workspaces and credentials.
Avoid copying raw outputs between agents.
Redact financial and licensed fields before transfer.
Check one workflow for shared mounts or synced folders.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data boundaries.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenBBTerminal cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses, and pathway likewise has no write, shell, or git capabilities. With no overlapping mutable write surface documented, there is no plausible capability conflict between the pair in the current profiles.
conditions: IF either profile is updated to grant shared write access to the same directory, conflict risk would need reassessment.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only.
Avoid shared mutable directories.
Recheck profiles after any permission change.

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenBBTerminal can emit financial analysis through APIs/MCP, and pathway is a document-processing system that could consume those outputs as inputs. The profiles do not show a verification gate in pathway, so if OpenBBTerminal’s output is treated as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream documents or pipelines even though the pair is not directly action-taking.
conditions: IF pathway ingests OpenBBTerminal outputs without validation, cascading errors can propagate.
IF downstream consumers rely on pathway-produced documents as authoritative, the impact expands to multiple work products.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents.
Require schema validation on OpenBBTerminal outputs.
Mark generated fields as untrusted until checked.
Sample one end-to-end pipeline for error propagation.
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks.

E_compliance.rationale: OpenBBTerminal explicitly touches financial and licensed data, which can carry retention and licensing obligations, while pathway’s profile does not state any residency or retention controls. Because the pairwise compliance posture is undocumented and the data class is sensitive, uncertainty pushes this above low even though no direct residency mismatch is proven.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal data is routed into pathway storage or logs, retention and licensing obligations may diverge.
IF pathway is deployed with longer retention than OpenBBTerminal’s data handling expectations, compliance exposure increases.
mitigations: Minimize stored financial data.
Review retention settings in both systems.
Document licensing constraints for imported datasets.
Check one log sink for sensitive fields.
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion workflows.
